question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is** "started."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Started"** is the correct verb to use to fill in the blank.
 
• It is the past tense form of **"start,"** which means to begin or commence. (कुछ करना आरंभ करना)
 
 
• **Example**: *She **started**__ the painting yesterday.*
 
 
 
• This option fits the context of the sentence, as it suggests a sequence of actions.
 
• Grammatically, **"proceeded" **could also work, but it sounds more formal and less commonly used in everyday language.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.
 
• Correct passage:

The Great Depression was a severe __worldwide__ economic depression in the decade __preceding__ World War II. In most countries the depression __**started**__ in about 1929 and lasted until the late 1930s or early 1940s. It was the longest, most widespread, and deepest depression of the 20th century. In the 21st century, the Great Depression is commonly used as an example of how far the world's economy can ______ (4) ______ .The depression originated in the U.S. Economic historians usually ______ (5) ______ the start of the Great Depression to the sudden devastating collapse of US stock market prices on 29 October 1929, known as Black Tuesday; some dispute this conclusion, and see the stock crash as a symptom, rather than a cause, of the Great Depression. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "Followed"** suggests to come, go or happen after somebody/something. (किसी व्‍यक्ति या वस्‍तु के पीछे आना, जाना या होना)
 
• **Option 3: "Proceeded"** is a valid verb choice, but it sounds more formal than "started." It means to continue doing something; to continue being done. (कुछ करना जारी रखना; कोई बात होते रहना)
 
• **Option 4: "Ended"** is the opposite of what the sentence is suggesting, as it implies that the actions have already finished. It means (to cause something) to finish. (समाप्‍त होना या करना)
